Based on the supplied October 2026 search results, **the BLUETTI AC200L is my top choice** for an RV because it combines a direct 30-amp-style RV connection, substantial solar charging capability and a price below $900. <Cite refs={["turn269673view0"]}/>

The important caveat: its 2,400W inverter supplies approximately 20A at 120V, not the full 30A available from an RV campground hookup.

**Best value:** Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO at $676.16. It also has a TT-30 outlet and 2,048Wh capacity, making it compelling if price matters most.

**Best alternative:** Renogy PowerStation 2000 at roughly $799–$849, with a TT-30 outlet and UPS capability.

## What will it actually power in an RV?

A 2,048Wh battery might provide approximately 1,700–1,850Wh of usable AC energy after inverter losses.

| RV appliance | Approximate runtime |
|---|---|
| 60W fridge average draw | 28–31 hours |
| 100W combined essentials | 17–18.5 hours |
| 500W appliance | 3.4–3.7 hours |
| 1,000W appliance | 1.7–1.85 hours |

These are estimates, not measured runtimes. A rooftop air conditioner may exceed the station's continuous or startup power limits, and even a compatible smaller AC will drain the battery quickly.

## Where to buy

The supplied results list a BLUETTI official-store checkout link with the discount code applied:

<Link url="https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l" title="BLUETTI AC200L — reported $854.05 checkout"/>

This is an affiliate redirect, and I haven't independently verified the final checkout price.

**My recommendation:** Choose the **BLUETTI AC200L** if solar charging and RV integration are your priorities. Choose the **Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO** if you want the strongest capacity-per-dollar value and would rather save approximately $178.

One question would help narrow this further: **Are you trying to run your RV's rooftop air conditioner, or mainly the refrigerator, lights, water pump and outlets?** That distinction could change which power station is best.
